Plaintiff further pleaded that, Section 38-A of the BDA Act 1976 reads that, "38-A. Grant of area reserved for civil amenities etc., (1) The Authority shall have the power to lease,
sell or otherwise transfer any area reserved for civic amenities for the purpose for which such area is reserved.
(2) The Authority shall not sell or otherwise dispose of any area reserved for public parks and playgrounds and civic amenities, for any other purpose and any disposition so made shall be null void.

Provided that where the allottee commits breach of any of the  6 O.S.No.2847/2017 conditions of allotment, the authority shall have the right to resume such site after affording an opportunity of being heard to such allottee".

The civic amenity site is land specified for the purpose of benefit of general public and the said land is held by the plaintiff in trust and therefore, it cannot be divested for any other use except for the purpose for which it was reserved.

The schedule property was not converted into general site and therefore it could not have been granted as alternative site under resolution and therefore such transaction made by the plaintiff is void ab-initio.

Therefore, it is necessary to declare that the sale deed dated 9.5.2013 executed in favour of defendant No.1 as null and void and consequently the sale deed dated 31.7.2013 executed in favour of defendant No.2 and 3 and sale deed dated 13.1.2014 executed by the defendant No.2 and 3 in favour of defendant No.4 has to be held as void.

Counsel for defendant No.4 argued that, as could be seen from the pleadings and evidence on record that the plaintiff has failed to seek for cancellation of the said sale deeds which should have been done by it within a period of three years from the date on which the right to sue first accrued i.e. on 9.5.2013 as prescribed under Article 58 of the Limitation Act.
As per Explanation of Section 3 of T.P.Act, in case of registered document, there is constructive notice.
Hence, the Limitation starts from the date of registration.

Explanation of Section 3 of T.P.Act reads as under:
 Explanation 1-Where any transaction relating to  immovable property is required by law to be and has  been effected by a registered instrument, any person  acquiring such property or any part of, or share or  interest in, such property shall be deemed to have  notice of such instrument as from the date of  registration or, [where the property is not all situated  in one sub-district, or where the registered  instrument has been registered under sub-section (2)
 of section 30 of the Indian Registration Act, 1908 (16  of 1908), from the earliest date on which any  memorandum of such registered instrument has been  filed by any Sub-Registrar within whose sub-district  any part of the property which is being acquired, or of  the property wherein a share or interest is being  acquired, is situated:]
As the plaintiff has not filed the suit within a period of three years from the date of the sale deed dated 9.5.2013, the suit of the plaintiff is hopelessly barred by law of limitation.
Hence, Issue No.4 is answered in the Affirmative.
